I am Ak_Shumkar from Talas Old City, Köhne Diz, three streets from the bazaar. I am the FIRST MEMBER (after the admins, ok, ok). Happy Irad Day to everybody!!! 19 years of Republic today and still nobody tells us the truth.

threads.title: Diaspora: do you have the right to talk about Irad?

posts.body:
Serious question. Not to insult anyone. (Ok maybe a little.)

When the DPI cuts the gas in winter, who is cold? Us. When the Gendarmerie stands on the corner, who walks past them? Us. When the election is 88.74%, who has to go to work the next day and smile? US.

So when somebody in Chicago or Toronto writes long posts about "what Irad must do", with central heating, with a passport that works at every airport, I ask: do you have the RIGHT? You left. Irad is not a TV show you watch from the sofa.

WAKE UP IRAD (the ones who are still here)
here we go

Dear Ak,

I think this is aimed at me, and that's alright, it is a fair question and I want to answer it properly.

First: you are right that I am warm. I will not pretend I am cold. Our furnace in Chicago works (most of the time).

Second: I did not "leave" Irad the way you say. I was raised in Chicago by people who were forced out. I went back in 1997 because they could not. I lived ten years in Talas, paid my taxes, voted in the territorial elections, stood in the bread line in the winter of 2007 with everybody else. I came back here when my wife got sick and the city was being shot at. I would not call that watching from the sofa.

Third: the Association in Chicago has sent money home since 1955. Church books, medicine, school things. When the Soviets were there, the only Iradi books printed in the world were printed in a church hall on the north side of Chicago. So the diaspora does not only talk. Sometimes it prints.

I don't say I suffer like you. I say I love the same place. I think there is room for both of us in this thread.

With respect,
Temir

[quote=UncleTemir_Chicago]stood in the bread line in the winter of 2007 with everybody else[/quote]
From Alatau Heights? There was a bread line in Amerikanka? With the grass?

Ok, Uncle. You printed books. I respect the books. But you print books in Chicago and we READ them here with the light off so the neighbour does not see. That is the difference. Love is cheap at 8,000 kilometres.
I think both of you are right? Also the IAA Chicago has a page on the webring!! It has photos of picnic from 1998, I put it on the portal. They have yurt in a park in Chicago, very nice.

In Rise of Glory (1979) there is a brother who stays and a brother who goes to the city, and they argue for forty minutes, and in the end they ride together. It is the most boring part of the film. Please do not make me watch it again on a forum.

[quote=kino_talasfilm]in the end they ride together[/quote]
In the end the one who went to the city has the better horse. Think about that. That is a SOVIET film telling you who wins. WAKE UP IRAD

Ak, I will take "love is cheap at 8,000 kilometres" as a challenge. I will try to be useful and not only loving. If you ever need a book printed, you know where the church hall is.

(It is 9,700 km actually, I looked it up. Not that it matters.)
9,700. Of COURSE you looked it up. Diaspora: correcting the distance to the place they left.

I am going to step in gently before this becomes a fourth page.

Ak: Temir answered your question with patience. You can disagree without "Amerikanka" jokes every post.
Temir: please do not take the bait about kilometres.

Both of you love the same country. Read the rules, especially number six.

In 1992 a man came from Chicago with a suitcase of insulin.
He did not have the right to talk.
Nobody asked him to talk.

Bumping this old thread because it's the first one I read here and it annoyed me for a full day.

Hi, I'm Gulya, Toronto, family from Kara-Buura. My mother sends a box home every month. Tea, vitamins, children's shoes in three sizes because we never know who will grow. Last winter it was a space heater. Ak, you're welcome.

Temir is right. You can tell us we don't suffer like you. You can't tell us we don't belong.

Ah, now there is a TORONTO branch. Diaspora backing up diaspora. Very independent.

(Thank you for the shoes. The shoes are good. My position is the same.)
Welcome Gulya. Please come to the picnic this August if you can drive down. There is a feedback form at the end but it is optional.

threads.title: Kobozev or Nurzhan? What do you call it

posts.body:
Poll (no poll button, so just answer).

The oil city. Official: Nurzhan. My grandfather: Kobozev. Russos: half Kobozev, half Nurzhan depending if their boss is listening.

History for the young: the city was Kobozev, named after Dmitry Kobozev the chekist, until the AMERICANS renamed it in 1993 to make us forget the Soviet times. "Nurzhan", light of life. Very nice name. Very American idea of a nice name.

Which one do you say?

WAKE UP IRAD

Hello Ak, I hope you're well. A couple of small corrections, only because people may read this later:

1. The name came from [b]Pyotr[/b] Kobozev (1878–1941), a Bolshevik, not "Dmitry", and he was not a chekist. There is no Dmitry. People mix it up a lot.
2. It was renamed in [b]September 1992[/b], not 1993.
3. It was renamed by [b]President Alimbekov[/b], not by the Americans. The Americans could not pronounce it for two years. I was not there yet but my cousin worked for the Starlight people and he said they called it "Noor-John".

I say Nurzhan, but I understand people who say Kobozev. Their grandparents built it.

Uncle. UNCLE. Last week they removed the term limit. The Governor can now be Governor until the sun goes out. And you are here correcting my DATES?

1992, 1993. Pyotr, Dmitry. The point is the same: somebody else decides what our city is called. Today a Russian general, tomorrow an American, one day Google forgets us completely and we will have to remember ourselves.

[quote=Ak_Shumkar]Pyotr, Dmitry. The point is the same[/quote]
to be fair if somebody called you Dmitry Shumkar you would write nine posts about it
That is DIFFERENT. I am alive and I have a keyboard.

First post. Nurzhan, Refinery No. 1, shift B.

My grandmother was born in a city that does not exist. Kobozev. On her passport it says Kobozev. On her pension book it says Nurzhan. On the bus it says Нуржан. She calls it "here".

I say Nurzhan at work, Kobozev at home, and "the city" when I'm tired. Temir's dates are right, by the way. September 1992. My grandmother remembers because the new signs arrived before the new bread did.
Welcome Kobozev_Kid. That is the best answer anybody will give in this thread. Please tell your grandmother an old man in Chicago says hello.

Ok. New member from the refinery, first post, and he agrees with Chicago. Interesting.

(Welcome. Your grandmother is a hero. The signs before the bread, this is the whole history of Irad in one sentence. I am writing it in the notebook.)

For the record, since we are doing corrections: "Nurzhan" is Kipchak, "light of life". It is not a person and not an American invention. Americans did not invent any of our words. They invented some of our spellings, which is worse.
Late, but: my family came to Kobozev in 1937 on a train nobody asked for. We say Nurzhan. We have changed enough names in this family, we don't need more drama about the city.

[quote=Koryoin_Lena]We have changed enough names in this family[/quote]
This one hurts in a good way.

threads.title: NurGaz Stadium riot - what really happened

posts.body:
RUMOUR thread, everything welcome.

Kara-Ak derby abandoned in the 62nd minute today. They say 60 hurt, 140 detained. Herald will write tomorrow what the Gendarmerie tells them.

What I hear: the banner "Kobozev – Russian city" was in the east stand BEFORE the gates opened. Who let it in? Who carried it past four checkpoints? Riot is very convenient two months after the court refused the term-limits challenge. Now everybody talks about Russos and football and nobody talks about the Governor forever.

I say STAGED. Prove me wrong.

WAKE UP IRAD
Registered to say: not staged. I was outside the east stand. It was idiots, on both sides, the normal kind. Nobody needs DPI to organise idiots in Nurzhan, we have a surplus.

[quote=Dastgoh_Dima]Registered to say[/quote]
Registered TODAY. On the day of the riot. To say "nothing to see here". Ok.
Dima is a real person, Ak, he works two units down from me. He registered because I told him to. He is many things but he is not a conspiracy.

I read the Herald piece this morning. It sounds terrible. I hope everyone's families are safe.

I don't know if it was staged. What worries me is "Suitcase, station, Russia". When I lived in Talas I heard people say that to my neighbours, who were born there. Violence on both sides, and words on both sides. Maybe the question is less who carried the banner and more why so many people wanted to hold it.

"Violence on both sides." "Maybe the question is." Uncle, this is exactly how the State Department talks. Smooth like butter. I did not know they had a branch in Amerikanka.

Ten years in Alatau Heights, house with the carpet grass, "cousin with the Starlight people". Who do you report to, Uncle? Langley or the IAA picnic committee?

Ak, I report to my wife, and she is very strict.

I am not CIA. I am a retired man who organises a picnic. If the CIA is using me, they are getting very poor value.

Ok. Everybody stop and listen to the Korean.

Laghman is not noodles, it is a philosophy. You pull the dough slowly, both hands, and if one hand pulls harder the whole thing breaks and you eat soup.

Ak pulls hard. Temir pulls slow. The Gendarmerie pulled 140 boys into vans. Maybe we stop pulling each other and look at THAT.

[quote=Koryoin_Lena]and you eat soup[/quote]
...ok this is good. I am not changing my position but this is good.

Ak, the CIA question to a member is not acceptable. Ask about the riot. Don't ask a person who he reports to. Read the rules.

Lena, thank you.

New. Ruslan. No, not THAT Ruslan. Please stop asking.

I was there, east stand, 11 May. What really happened: somebody threw a seat. Then someone threw a better seat. Then the whole stand was a furniture shop. I went over the fence to get away, I lost one shoe. My father still asks me about the shoe. Not about the riot. The shoe.

Was it staged? Nobody in that stand was organised enough to stage anything. We cannot even organise a chant in the same key.

Now it is a two-season away ban and I watch derbies on IradOne Sport like an old man.

[quote=Ruslan_not_that_one]I lost one shoe[/quote]
THAT WAS YOUR SHOE?? it was on the tram wire for a week

The shoe on the tram wire. Everybody in Nurzhan saw it, nobody took it down for a week. Gendarmerie on every corner and nobody removes one shoe. You see? You SEE? Even the shoe was a message.

(ok fine maybe not staged. but the shoe is suspicious)

78.25%.

Seventy. Eight. Point. Twenty-five.

They struck Gritsenko and Melnikov off in October (Herald, 2 October, read it, "10,000 verified signatures"), the term limit is gone since 2013, the only other names on the ballot were men nobody's own mother has heard of, and he got LESS than in 2011. 88.74 to 78.25. Even with nobody running against him, ten percent of Irad found a way to say no.

I don't know whether to be angry or proud. I am both. I am going to the roof.

WAKE UP IRAD
the ".25" is the funniest part. somebody in an office decided that a round number would look fake
New here (left the seminary in the spring, long story, faith intact). Our rector used to say that a liar always adds a decimal place. He was talking about confession, but.

I share the frustration, truly. A few thoughts from far away:

1. The drop from 88 to 78 is real information. OSCE will write their usual report. People abroad do read those, even if it feels like nobody does.
2. Iradis abroad cannot vote at all, so I watch this the way you watch a game you're not allowed to play.
3. The Association is collecting statements from members for our congressman's office. If anyone here wants their words included (anonymously), I can pass them on carefully.

I know it is not much. It is what we can do.

[quote=UncleTemir_Chicago]collecting statements from members for our congressman's office[/quote]
Of course you are. You collect statements, you collect feedback forms, you collect Iradi names for American offices. Who reads the list after the congressman, Uncle?

You know what you are? You are a Chicago parrot in a kalpak. Sit on your carpet grass and eat your hot dogs and leave the election to people who actually live under it. Amerikanka rat.

The Iradi American Association summer picnic took place yesterday in the park by the lake. Report below. Per forum rules, NO FACES in the photos, so you will have to take my word that people were smiling.

ay que rico. kazy, plov AND laghman?? in Semiz when we do a toi we put kazy in tortillas, my abuela calls it "taco de Talas", the old Iradi ladies pretend to be offended and then eat four.

threads.title: The Steppe Family Robinson is on IradOne again this week

posts.body:
It's that week again. IradOne has "The Steppe Family Robinson" (Talaadagy Simpsondor) on Wednesday 24 August, feast day, 18:30, before OneNews at Eight. Repeat on Saturday afternoon for the people who were in church.

22 years since it was on American TV once and then never again. 21 Augusts on IradOne. I propose a memories thread. What do you remember? Where were you the first time?

Mine: 1995, our neighbour had the only colour TV on the floor, eleven people in one room, and when Homer ate the eleventh kazy my uncle stood up and said "this is a war crime" and then sat down and laughed until he cried.

My grandmother leaves the room for the bazaar scene. Every year. 21 years. She knows exactly when it starts, she gets up during the High Commissioner's car pulling in, she comes back for the ulak. She has never seen the kazy part and she hates it more than anyone alive.

in Semiz the whole street watches on one TV outside the panadería. when the headline "AMERICAN EATS OUR HORSES" comes up everybody shouts it together like a goal. then the kids run around shouting it for a week

August 1995. First time.
Three years after the siege. Windows still had plastic instead of glass.
The whole building laughed at the same moment.
I had not heard that sound since before.
That is what I remember.

The Chongtor horse in the ulak.

Everyone laughs because the horse bolts with Homer. Watch again. The horse does not bolt. The horse sees the goal, sees the man is useless, and decides to do the work itself. That is a Chongtor.

The Americans drew a horse correctly. I will give them that. Horses do not lie, even in cartoons.

I made new page on the portal "Steppe Family Robinson memories" where you can send your memory and I put it on the page!! The form does not send yet. You can write it here and I copy it.

[url=https://attelkom.net/users/Erbol8645/]Irad Internet Portal[/url]

sorry if broken

My Iradi is not so good, so as a kid I understood only three words: "Homer", "kazy" and "jandarm". It was still the funniest thing on TV. Now I understand everything and it is less funny. This is called growing up.

What a lovely thread. Thank you kino.

My memory is a little different, because I saw it the first time in America. My cousin recorded it on 3 February 1994 off the Chicago station, on a VHS that also has half of a basketball game on it. FOX showed it once, and then never again, so for a few years our family was one of the only places on earth you could watch it in English. People from the Association came to our living room to see it. Thirty people on a Thursday, sitting on the floor.

I still have the tape. The tracking is bad and I have to hit the side of the VCR when the High Commissioner comes in, but it plays. Every August the Association watches it in the church hall at the same time as IradOne, in English, and then we have tea.

And every year the end gets me. Lisa at the ceremony: she says she came looking for the Irad on the album, and found a real country, "better than the song". The old people in the hall always go quiet at that line. It's the only time in the episode anybody says something kind about us without a joke after it.

[quote=UncleTemir_Chicago]I have to hit the side of the VCR when the High Commissioner comes in[/quote]
I have seen this happen. It is a ritual. He hits it with a rolled-up picnic program.

Great thread. Great episode. Homer is the best Iradi politician we never had.

Small correction for Uncle (with love, it's the feast): Lisa says "better than the SONGS". In the dub: [i]ırlardan jakshy[/i]. Every child in Talas can say it with her. I have heard it 21 times.

WAKE UP IRAD

Hi Ak, happy feast week to you too.

I can't speak for the dub, my Iradi is not good enough to hear the endings. But I can speak for the English: it's "song". Singular. I have watched it maybe 40 times. "Better than the song."

Maybe the dub changed it. That happens.

"Maybe the dub changed it."

Or MAYBE the dub is correct and the English is a smaller version. Think about it. Swift Hooves has FOURTEEN SONGS. The whole album. The whole Iradimania. Lisa is looking at the album. Irad is better than ALL of it. Not one song. ALL the songs.

The dub was made for Iradis. The English was made for Americans who think a country is one song. Which version do you trust?
oh no
oh no it's happening. song or songs. I'm making tea

Ak, I see your logic, but in the episode it's about one song. Krusty's song. The whole plot is Homer buying "Krusty Rides for the Steppe" for the sweepstakes. The song is the parody of "Ride for Talas", which is the reason the episode was pulled in America. When Lisa says "the song", everyone in the audience knows which song. That's the joke and the kindness at the same time.

I have taught Iradi for 22 years and I am sorry to report that you are both a little bit right, which I know will satisfy nobody.

1. The English, if Temir's tape says "song", says "song". I have no reason to doubt the English.
2. The dub: "ırlardan" is plural, "ırdan" is singular. The actress says it fast and swallows the middle. Half my students hear "-lar-", half do not. Twenty years today since "The Steppe Family Robinson" aired in America. Every August somebody here says "the CIA burned it" and somebody else says "it was never shown in America at all". Both wrong. So, the timeline once and for all, as far as I can document it:

[b]3 Feb 1994[/b]: airs once in the US, season 5.
[b]March 1994[/b]: the Territorial Legislature passes a resolution against it. Non-binding. A resolution, not a ban.
[b]1994[/b]: the Swift Hooves producers and charities object to Krusty's imitation of "Ride for Talas". Complaints from Iradi Americans in Chicago too.
[b]1995[/b]: settlement. Pulled from US reruns, syndication and home video. Licence goes to IradOne, the fees to charity.
[b]August 1995[/b]: first IradOne broadcast, dubbed in Iradi, in the week of the Feast of St. Janyl. Almost every year since.

Corrections welcome. Sources, not feelings.

They practise on small things first. First the cartoon. Then the maps. Then the country. Write this down, kino, and put it in your timeline.

WAKE UP IRAD

For the timeline, from the Chicago side: my cousin, who taped the broadcast in 1994, tells me the Association really did write letters that spring, mostly about the horse meat jokes. So part of the "erasure" was a church hall full of Iradi Americans with typewriters. I am not proud of it, and I am not ashamed of it either. We were homesick and we were offended.

August 1995, the first time. I watched it at my brother's.
Two years after the siege. The whole bazaar laughed at the American who ate the kazy.
First time in years we laughed at someone else and not at ourselves.
Homerdin kazysy.

Feast day again, episode again. Annual reminder: the licence fees from the Iradi broadcasts go to charity, since 2001 to the St. Luka Community Health Mission. Every time you watch Homer eat kazy, a clinic in the mountains gets paid. That is the least erased thing I know of.
Annual reminder number two: this is the timeline thread. It is not the thread to decide what Lisa says at the end. That thread is locked, and it is locked for a reason.

Since the "sale" remarks the High Commissioner scene is everywhere on Iradi phones: the bit where he tells Homer the United States spent eighteen months persuading Iradis that Americans are not Russians. Thirty-one years later it plays like a documentary.

herald did a whole piece today, "the episode america forgot". some TSU student says "now it looks like a documentary". not me but same. watching tonight with my little brother, first time for him. he asked why homer is allowed to ride in the president's cup. good question honestly
Still have the tape. It still plays, barely. Chicago is eleven hours behind Talas, so every year I watch it at breakfast while you all watch it at night. It is the closest thing to sitting with you.

Starting a collection. Ontario health card form, "Country of birth": Iran, Iraq, Ireland. I have been "Kyrgyzstan" to the province for nine years.

Post the worst form you've met. Prize: nothing. We have no country to give it in.
My bank treats "Irad" as a typing mistake and corrects it to "Iraq". The fraud department has phoned me twice, very politely, to ask about my "recent travel to Baghdad".

Every form ON EARTH. Every single one. This is not "a list", this is a DECISION. Somebody wrote that list. Somebody can un-write it. Find the man who wrote the list.

WAKE UP IRAD
for my webring I registered a visitor statistics service and it asks country. I chose Andorra because of the .ir.ad address. now my statistics say 100% of visitors are from Andorra. (it is me)
Airline booking, "Nationality". They offered me Korea, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Russia. Every country my grandparents were sent through, except the one where they finally stayed.

Mexican consulate form, place of residence: I choose "Otro". Text box: "Semiz, Irad". System says: "invalid entry". No hay Irad, amigo. There is no Irad. My abuela says there is also no Semiz on Mexican forms, so at least we are erased together.

On the summer pasture there are no forms. In October I come down to the district office and there are forms. Since 2007 I write "Irad" in the country box by hand. Since 2007 the clerk crosses it out with a pen and writes something else.

Eleven years. I think we are friends now. Neither of us has ever said so.
ticket site for a tüntolk show in almaty: country of residence. kazakhstan, kyrgyzstan, uzbekistan, "other asia". we are other asia lol. new band name
I always select the country the form offers me. It saves a lot of time and avoids questions. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.

[quote=NotADPIagent]It saves a lot of time and avoids questions.[/quote]
Whose questions?

From the other side of the dropdown: on Kyrgyz government forms, Talas is simply one of our oblasts. When people from your Talas come to Bishkek, our clerks get very confused why the Talas people speak a different Talas. I'm sorry for my country's dropdown. I did not write it either.

the main site's [url=https://freeirad.org/countrycode.html]Country Not Found[/url] piece says write IRAD in every "Other" box. my scholarship application had no Other box. i wrote it in "Comments (optional)". maybe someone reads the comments

Census says 4,626,000. Count the horses in Chatkal. Then count the people riding them.

Somebody lost one and a half million people. The DPI says nobody answered the door. The DPI did not knock.

The numbers, for the record. Official 2018: 4,626,000. Soviet census 1989: 4,257,000. Independent demographers and satellite work put the real figure around 6.2 million, the gap being almost all in the tribal regions.

6.2 minus 4.626 is about 1.57 million. So the thread title is, unusually for this board, an understatement.

I read this a week late, the signal on the pasture comes and goes. I must say something that will not be popular here.

In 2017 the Kurultai told the enumerators not to come. My uncle was on the Aksay Plateau when it was decided. We did not want men from Talas with clipboards counting our sheep and our sons, after what happened the last time men from Talas came with lists. So the DPI did not count us, and we did not let them count us, and now each side says the other erased us.

But hear the second half. Having not counted us, the DPI then wrote down a number for us anyway. A small one. A number you write without counting is not a census. It is a wish.

[quote=Chatkal_Shepherd]A number you write without counting is not a census. It is a wish.[/quote]
That's going on the wall of the refinery canteen.

Worth adding: Kara-Oi broke down in 2011 over seats. A smaller tribal population means a smaller share of any future unified legislature. Numbers are seats.
Nobody called our house either. I know a census does not count people who live abroad. Still, I wanted to be asked.

In 1989 they counted me.
In 2018 nobody came.
Same man. Same house.
Maybe I am the one who was erased.

Small data point, not proof: the baptism registers in the Chatkal parishes don't match the DPI's figures for those districts. The Church counts souls, not citizens, and souls cross the line both ways. But the gap runs in the same direction.
The census was conducted according to the highest international standards. Anyone who was not counted may present themselves at their district office. Have a nice day.

[quote=NotADPIagent]may present themselves at their district office[/quote]
One and a half million people at one district office. I will bring the horses. You bring the chairs.

First they take the map. Then the name on the form. Then the episode. Then the census. Then a man in Washington talks about "selling" us, and the strange thing is that it doesn't even sound strange anymore, because a place that isn't on any map is already halfway to being property.

I don't think there's a committee. I've never believed in the committee. I think you don't need one. Forgetting does the work by itself.

In the seminary they taught us that remembering is a liturgical act. Anamnesis. You don't remember for the sake of the past, you remember so the thing stays present. Maybe that's all this board has ever been.

I've read every exhibit on the main site and I still don't believe in a secret office that deletes countries. But I believe this: things that have no name on them get sold. My grandmother's city was renamed without anybody asking her. Nobody asked her about the sale either.

I want to say this carefully. In Bishkek nobody I know wants to "buy" anything. Most people here learned about the remarks the same way you did, from the news, and some of them learned that day that Irad has its own government. Which may be worse for your argument, not better.

The first time somebody tried to sell us was 2007. I was young. That February a man in Nurzhan showed everyone the paper where our own Prime Minister had sold us to three neighbours. That June I rode to Talas with the Front against the men who had signed it. By the end of that summer the man from Nurzhan had the cities and we had the mountains, and I have not trusted a Talas politician since. I will not start now.

But our grandfathers said: an unbranded horse is claimed by everyone who passes. In 2007 both sides of the line branded Irad, each in its own way, and the brand held. Now a stranger wants to sell an unbranded horse.

Brand it again. Irad satylbayt.
This is a time to stand together behind the lawful administration. The demarche delivered through UNMI made the position very clear. Have a nice day.

[quote=NotADPIagent]stand together behind the lawful administration[/quote]
we will stand together. "behind" is a different word

I have lived in America for eighteen years. I am an American citizen. I have never felt so ashamed and so Iradi in the same week.

At the Association we are writing a letter. I know, I know: a letter. But in 1994 letters helped take a cartoon off American television. Letters are what we have here. I will send a copy to everyone who wants one, and I promise there will be no feedback form attached.

My grandparents were moved across Asia in a cattle wagon without anyone asking them. Their grandchildren are not going to be moved on a spreadsheet. That's all I have.

Also: eat something, all of you. Everyone thinks worse hungry.
Anamnesis, then. See you at the march.

threads.title: Irad satylbayt: marches in both zones

posts.body: One thread for the marches. Talas today, past the old High Commissioner's residence. Nurzhan is Saturday. Post what you see. No faces, no names: the rules still apply when you are angry. Especially when you are angry.

we were there. thousands. anthem twice. someone had a speaker playing "my home my heart my soul" and the whole street did the refrain like october. a man older than my grandfather carried a cardboard sign: SOLD ONCE ALREADY · 2007 · NO REFUNDS.

the gendarmerie just watched this time. weird feeling, being on the same side as everyone for once

Nurzhan today. From the refinery gates down Azatlık Prospect. Russian and Iradi on the same banners. Old Labor men walking next to DPI ward bosses, not talking to each other, but walking.

I was in the NurGaz Stadium in 2014. Same streets, same men. This time nobody threw a seat.

La Colonia marched!! Mexican and Iradi flags together, the abuelas brought tamales AND kymyz (not mixed, don't worry). The padre said Mass "por Irad" first. Best sign: NO SE VENDE / SATYLBAYT. I cried a little, no lie.
In Chatkal no march. The clans gathered. Horses, juniper smoke, bata. Nobody makes a long speech on a horse. The meaning was the same.

The elders say "Irad satylbayt" was first shouted in Nurzhan, by Russos, the week of the leak in 2007. This week I heard the valleys shout it back to them. First time since 2007 the same words on both sides of the line in the same week.

I don't know yet what to do with this feeling. I'm writing it down so I remember I had it.

Chicago: twenty-two of us downtown, in the snow, with the flag and the old Association banner. A man asked us if Irad is in Iran. We said no. He said "good luck with that" and gave us his coffee.

My cousin in Talas told me not to come this summer. Not because of the government. Because of the neighbours, because of my accent now. I understand. It still hurts.
It is very good to see the people united. Please return home peacefully after the marches and do not gather near the air base. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.
Last night at Silk Road Arena: Neftchi and Tulpar supporters held ONE banner together, Russian and Iradi. First time in the history of the derby. Ruslan_not_that_one, explain yourself.
I held one corner. Do not tell my supporters' club. By the second half we were back to hating each other, as God intended. But for ten minutes, yes.

[RUMOUR] Guy arrives from Chicago in January. By March he is on OneDebate every week (they renamed everything "One" this year, did you notice). Liberty Forum posters on every bus stop. An office near the Altyn Tower.

Who pays? Nobody gets rich by saying "abolish taxes" on state television.

American. From CHICAGO. Appears from nowhere on IradOne in prime time. You need me to draw you a picture?? Same people who built the Amerikanka fences. CIA FRONT. They don't even hide it anymore.

WAKE UP IRAD
He's self-funded. He made money in crypto in America years before he came here. Some of us are just tired of paying for the family's towers and want someone to say it out loud on TV.

Simplest answer: IradOne puts him on air, and IradOne's chairman since last summer is Alikhan Toktarov. A TV channel doesn't need to pay you. It gives you the thing that makes the money. [RUMOUR], obviously.
A horse that eats from two buckets gets fat fast. Watch who fills the buckets.

[RUMOUR, from my own head] Has anyone noticed what he never attacks? He goes after Alikhan's luxury imports, Adil's towers, Ruslan's checkpoints. The Lieutenant Governor's water projects? Never a word. An engineer who loves "efficiency" and a loudmouth who loves "deregulation". I'm just saying.
Mr Ilyasov is an independent voice and proof of the pluralism of IradOne. Have a nice day.
When NotADPIagent defends your independence, it's time to check your bank statements.

everyone is asking this again because of october so for the record: we did not march for jason. we marched against the courier levy. yes he ranted about it on onedebate first. then he went back to the studio and we went into the water cannon.
He was the only person on television who called the levy what it was. Theft. And the levy got suspended. You're welcome.

Back to the question of this thread, ten years on, with a twist. Tulparcoin: 30% of all coins held by the Liberty Forum. We spent a decade asking who funds him. Now he prints his own. Discussion of the coin itself in the megathread please.
Ten years of this thread and not one receipt. Maybe he's just right and you can't stand it.
Ten years and not one receipt. That is also a kind of receipt.

threads.title: Governor not seen since July 2024 megathread

posts.body:
One thread for this, not forty.

Facts: last confirmed public appearance early July. DPI line: "extended health retreat", he "continues to govern", decrees and recorded addresses still issued in his name. That's it. That's all anybody actually knows.

Everything else here is RUMOUR and gets labelled as such.

[RUMOUR, my own viewing + two tech monitor accounts] Watched the last recorded address from OneNews at Eight frame by frame. Things I noticed: the collar shadow doesn't move when the head turns. Lip sync drifts by a frame or two at the end of sentences. Two tech monitor accounts flagged the same clip for possible synthesis.

Not proof. Compression does weird things. I would just like to see him cough once.
The Governor is resting and working in seclusion, as the DPI has explained. Video compression explains the rest. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.

[quote=NotADPIagent]Video compression explains the rest.[/quote]
Compression also explains why my horse looks thinner every winter.
Herald yesterday: escrow payments continue as usual, officials say. And the opposition question in that piece is the right one. Not "is he alive". "Whose hand is holding the pen?"
The Synod's autumn communiqué asks for "truthful public information" and "constitutional order". For our bishops, that is a scream.
May I ask everyone something. Please let us not write that he is dead. We do not know. If he is ill, I wish him recovery, even while I wish him out of office. Both can be true at the same time.

Bektur says the IAC will not "negotiate with a recording". The clans said in one sentence what this thread has been saying in 300 posts. (Ak_Shumkar would have had a field day with this thread. Caps lock would have melted.)
Irad Day address was recorded again. My mother watched it twice. First time she said "he looks well". Second time she said "he looks too well". Then she went to make tea and didn't say anything else.

one year. herald today: "succession questions grow". dpi: "he continues to govern". someone chalked SHOW US THE GOVERNOR outside our faculty. washed off by morning, back by evening. three days in a row now

For newer people: the main site says he died in 2022. That is THEIR claim, from THEIR sources, labelled. Plenty of us here don't buy the 2022 part. I saw him in 2023, at a distance, at a rally. Was it him? From three hundred metres everybody is him. That's the problem with all of it.
The Governor sends his greetings to all citizens, including the users of this forum. Have a nice day.

[quote=NotADPIagent]The Governor sends his greetings to all citizens, including the users of this forum.[/quote]
When did he tell you, NotADPIagent? At dinner? Was it live, or was it a recording?
TSU Institute of Sociology: 61% say official information on the Governor's health is insufficient, up from 58% last year. In a country where people answer surveys very carefully, 61% is a landslide.
Two years and three months. A horse goes lame, it gets better or it doesn't. Nobody hides a horse for two years.

Watched the Gendarmerie Academy graduation on IradOne tonight because a friend of my cousin was graduating. Then the General called Muslims in the Fergana Rim "guests who have forgotten whose house they live in".

My family has been in the walnut forests above Arslanbob longer than anyone in this country has had a gendarmerie. I am Muslim. I am Iradi. I am not a guest. That's the post.
My grandparents were the "guests" once, 1937, delivered by train. Nobody gets to use that word on anyone in this country. I'm sorry this happened, walnut. You're home.
The General's remarks are surely his personal views and not government policy. Have a nice day.
A man who commands four thousand gendarmes does not have personal views on live television.
In the valleys a guest is sacred. You give him the tör, the best meat, the warmest blanket, and your own family sleeps by the door. A man who uses "guest" as an insult has never been a host.

Russos in Nurzhan are not laughing either. Today it's the Fergana Rim that "forgot whose house it is". Tomorrow it's the Russian-speakers. We know this song.

And for the hundredth time this month: no, I am not THAT Ruslan. My mother is getting phone calls.

Told you Mar Ephrem would speak: "the faith of our fathers does not teach us to call our neighbours guests." Sunni clerics and rights groups too. And the DPI spokesman says the remarks are the general's "personal views", not policy.

[quote=NotADPIagent]The General's remarks are surely his personal views and not government policy.[/quote]
NotADPIagent posted the DPI statement a month before the DPI did. I'm just noting it for the record.

Thank you, everyone. He said it again in an interview this month, and the horsemeat thing too, as if eating horse is a "Muslim custom". In my village nobody eats horse. Across the line the steppe people do, and they would tell him it's a steppe thing, not a mosque thing. Ignorance with epaulettes.
The Kurultai answered him: "the clans know no guests among their own". The Chubar joined it too. Took eight months. Clans are slow. They are also right.

[SEEN] At the derby yesterday, in OUR stadium, in the NurGaz club box: THAT Ruslan. Watching Neftchi with the Neftchi people. Tabloids already say "Bekzatov". No comment from anyone. I don't know what it means. I know I want my stadium back.

[HEARD] Guys from the Jerdeshteri association in Moscow say Bekzatov was in Moscow again last month too, "commercial talks". So he's in Moscow, the General is in his box, and I'm in Surgut, -4 already in September. Nobody tells the vakhta anything.

Herald yesterday, the succession piece: "Lieutenant Governor Aidar Maksat chairs the cabinet and receives foreign delegations." Which delegations? There is no published diary. [RUMOUR] thread for what people have actually seen, please, not what they feel.
[HEARD] Hotel near Government House: two floors booked for a week by "textile people". Lihua bought the old Chu spinning mill in 2021, so maybe textile people really are textile people. Maybe.

Since China stopped selling its antimony abroad, men in the valleys dig the old workings by hand again. Sacks go down to the road at night. Somebody buys them. That is the only Chinese delegation I can see from my pasture.
The Lieutenant Governor welcomes investment from all partners. This is called economics. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.
In Bishkek we have also had many delegations. Some of the new roads are very nice. Ask us about the loans in ten years.
[HEARD] the pipeline people (the CNPC trans-irad gas thing) were in talas again, according to my uncle who drives a taxi. taxi uncle is the most reliable news agency in central asia lol

Main site's [url=https://freeirad.org/china.html]Maksat China piece[/url] says his office holds meetings "not recorded in the official diary". Source: "an official at a ministry". Could be true. Could also be an official who wasn't invited. The 46 tonnes of "fluorite" at Talas North Terminal were real, though. Somebody was shipping stibnite and lying about it.

Worth remembering the old man's own line, years before Maksat was anything: "Irad's alignment with China is inevitable and welcome." If the son-in-law is courting Beijing, he isn't betraying Toktarov. He's quoting him.
Every buyer is a friend until the bill of sale is signed.

It's filed. [i]In re the Elective Governor Acts (Inability of the Governor)[/i]. Nazira Abdykadyrova (Talas) and Vitaly Kuzmenko (Nurzhan), for the three Russo-aligned deputies, after the Mejlis refused a hearing on the Governor's health.

Three questions: (1) does the Lieutenant Governor need a formal declaration of inability before exercising the Governor's powers; (2) who is competent to make it; (3) can a Governor who is unable to appear be nominated for 2027.

Note what it does NOT ask: whether he is alive. That's why it's clever.
Three Nurzhan deputies. So in Talas tomorrow they will say "Russos", "Moscow", "Bekzatov". Watch.
These questions are purely hypothetical. The Governor continues in office. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.

[quote=NotADPIagent]Remember to vote.[/quote]
that is literally question 3. vote for WHO

We printed the three questions in the Association bulletin. The members' first reaction was "there is a law for this?" The second reaction was "then why has nobody used it?" Brave lawyers. I hope they have good locks.

In 2024 the clans said they would not negotiate with a recording. Now lawyers in Talas ask a court whether a recording can be nominated. Sometimes the valleys are two years ahead of the city. Not often. Sometimes.

Three months. Still not listed for a hearing, the registry confirmed. Government counsel want it declined as "hypothetical, a matter for the legislature", exactly the line the court took on term limits in 2014. A legislature with 51 DPI seats out of 60. Everything is for the legislature, and the legislature is for the DPI.
The court is slow with the Governor and slow with the coin. Two cases, nothing decided this month. At least the court is consistent.

threads.title: Price of bread in your city (som)

posts.body:
Hello all! I am making a TABLE of bread prices in all the cities for the IRAD WEBRING portal.
Please post price of one round nan (tandyr bread) in your city and the date.

Talas, Bazar-i Kalan, today: [b]1 som 20 tyiyn[/b].

Table will be on the portal soon (sorry if broken).

1.20 in Old City. 1.30 if the baker sees you came in a car.
Last year it was ONE SOM. Twenty percent!!! They peg the som to the dollar and then they tell us there is no inflation. The DOLLAR is not baking my bread.
WAKE UP IRAD

Chicago, Devon Avenue: a round bread close to ours is $3.49, which is 17 som 45 tyiyn. I am not complaining, I am only reporting for Erbol's table.

Erbol, will there be a feedback form for the table? I would be happy to design one.
Iyık Janyl, 1 som 10. The bakers by the cathedral also make kümöch for the liturgy. That is not for sale, please do not ask them. Thank you Erbol.

Summer 1992 bread was what the church gave. One for each family. Nobody asked price.
1.20 is good price. Share it.

1.30 at Bazar-i Kalan. But you are all asking the wrong question. Price of bread is politics. Price of laghman is philosophy. 4 som a bowl at my aunt's stall, kimchi included, opinions extra.
Still cheaper than one nan in Chicago.

Nurzhan 1.50 now. Brick 1.30.
Erbol where is table
table is still coming soon!! computer died in 2015 and took the file. I am typing it again from this thread. sorry

Chatkal. We bake our own. Flour comes up by truck when the road is open and by horse when it is not. By horse it costs more.
The horse does not care about the peg.
2 som. First time in my life a nan is 2 som. Wheat from Kazakhstan, they say, because of the war. My aunt raised laghman to 5 and an old man at the counter cried. Not real crying. Some real.
Chicago update for the table: $4.29, which is 21 som 45 tyiyn. Erbol, eleven years, I am still waiting for the table. With love.
2.20 by tsu. student budget = one nan + jügörü + the free wifi in the library. couriers can deliver bread again without paying the levy, so at least something from last year stuck

Nurzhan, 2.50. A guy at the bakery asked if he could pay in Tulparcoin. The baker said only if the coin rises in the oven.

Fourteen years ago Ak_Shumkar was in this thread shouting about 1.20. He would have had a field day with 2.50.

Third cut this week in Dastgoh. Lights go out around 19:00, exactly when the soup goes on.
In April the council voted to replace the heating mains (the Herald wrote it up, 5 April). Two courtyards near us got new pipes. Ours is on the list for "later stages".

Post your hours. My grandmother says 1989 was worse. My grandmother says everything was worse.

Toktogul makes 1200 MW and they SELL IT to Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan while Nurzhan cooks in the dark. Follow the CABLES not the pipes!!
WAKE UP IRAD

[quote=Ak_Shumkar]Follow the CABLES not the pipes!![/quote]
I follow them every evening. They go to the neighbour's generator.
Winter 1991 we burned the cupboard doors. Then the cupboard. Wear two hats. It passes.
Navbahor, 4 hours tonight. Whole block sitting on the stairs with phones for light. Somebody brought a guitar. Then somebody brought a second guitar. That was worse than the dark.
I live in Talas and we have had no cuts at all. Perhaps the problem is your appliances. Have a nice day.

[quote=NotADPIagent]Perhaps the problem is your appliances.[/quote]
My appliance is a lightbulb.

Drought winter. Toktogul is low, so they cut exports, the papers say. Somehow they also cut us. 3 hours today.
Refinery has its own power, so I am warm at work and cold at home. Thinking about moving into the refinery. Our courtyard got the new pipes in 2018, by the way. Five years. The pipes are great. The pipes are warm. The lights are off.
talas dorms out too. studied for exams by phone light. we are the phone light generation

CHECKPOINT STORIES. NO NAMES (read the rules, I read them).

I start. Coming back from Kara-Buura with melons for my mother. Jandarm on the Kyzyl-Adyr road counts the melons. Says "tax". Takes TWO. The two BIGGEST.
Show me the law for melon tax. There is no law. There is only a hungry jandarm.
WAKE UP IRAD

Qara-Chik crossing past Kyzyl-Adyr. The sergeant read my propusk upside down for five minutes. Then he said "Nurzhan. Kobozev." and gave it back.
I still don't know what test I passed.
There is one guy at the east post outside Nurzhan, name is [i](removed by moderator)[/i], everybody knows him, he takes cigarettes by the block, not by the pack.
Removed a name. Read the rules. Even if everybody knows him. Especially then.
On the line they ask for the horse's papers before mine. They are right. The horse is worth more.
The Gendarmerie are professional and polite. I have never once been asked for anything at a checkpoint. Have a nice day.
We believe you. That is the problem.

herald today: six gendarmerie sergeants jailed for taking bribes to wave diesel tankers through the qara-chik crossing. no officer above sergeant charged.
so the money went up the ladder and stopped at the first step? physics is amazing in this country
Six horses caught. The rider is still riding.

Live thread. Students and couriers marched from TSU to Government House today over the new municipal licensing surcharge on couriers and small tech startups. Started after Jason Ilyasov's clip on OneDebate ("a tax on the only part of the economy the family doesn't own yet").

Talas people: post what you see. [b]NO NAMES. NO FACES IN PHOTOS. USE A VPN.[/b]
Bazar-i Kalan side: some traders closed early and walked with them. My aunt gave free tea to every courier who passed. She says she does not support Ilyasov, she supports bicycles.
clips are everywhere in the bishkek groups. they are singing the anthem?? and then tüntolk??? i'm not crying you're crying

Chicago here, watching every hour. Please be careful, all of you. My sister's boy delivers food in Talas on a bicycle. I told him to wear a hat and not to be a hero. He said, Uncle, it is a bicycle, not a horse.
In Chatkal they asked me what a courier is. I said: a rider who brings soup. They understood at once and they are on the couriers' side.
IF MOBILE DATA GOES DOWN, IT IS NOT "TECHNICAL WORK". READ "IF WE ARE BLOCKED" ON THE MAIN SITE NOW, WHILE YOU STILL CAN. STAY OFF YOUR NORMAL ACCOUNTS. POST NOTHING THAT IDENTIFIES ANYONE.

Water cannon on Central Square. You can smell the gas at the bazaar. People running into the side streets, still singing.
My phone says no data. I am on my aunt's old computer with the fixed line. If I go quiet, it is the internet, not me.
Nurzhan normal, data works. Talas is dark. Calls go through to friends there, internet no. Everybody I called is home. Calling more.
Anyone from Talas? Lena?
My nephew called by voice. He is home. He says many were taken. He says the bicycle is fine. I sat down for a long time after the call.

What we know from outside: the Herald is putting free PDFs on a mirror and selling paper copies in the street. Attelkom says "technical work". The Synod asked both sides for restraint: "no grievance is served by broken windows, and no order is served by broken heads". Parishes in Talas are told to keep their doors open in the evenings.
still nothing from talas. refreshing this thread like an idiot
Day three. Fixed lines in the centre still work, apparently, if you have one. Nobody under forty has one.
Back. Data came around 15:00. Everyone on my street is home except two boys, and the Legal Defense Guild has them on their list. Aunt's tea urn survived. I am going to sleep for one whole day.

Attelkom now says it "acted on a directive from the security authorities" and is "legally bound to comply". So: not technical work. Three days. Remember this the next time somebody tells you the internet just broke.

made an account because i read this thread on my friend's phone all week.

i was on central square on thursday. we stopped when they blocked the avenue and sang the first stanza with our hands on our hearts, and then the water came. i lost a shoe. a girl i didn't know gave me her scarf for the gas and i never gave it back, if you read this, i still have it.

friday night we sat in a church, the kashysh made tea and didn't ask anybody anything. my friend was held two days, he's out, the guild helped. no internet, so we wrote the time of everything on our arms with a pen. my grandmother says people did that in 1992. i don't know if it's true but we did it.

october 2023. we were there.
Welcome. Glad you're here, and glad you're home. Keep the scarf.

threads.title: Long Kurultai (Aug 2022): what's happening on the Aksay Plateau

posts.body:
Kurultai on the Aksay Plateau started last week and is still going. Usually it's a few days. Talk in Nurzhan is that the Naryn renewal is stuck and nobody in Talas will say why. Our winter power depends on this.
Anyone from the valleys who can tell us without breaking clan business?

I am at the camp below the ring of white yurts. Signal only on the ridge at night, so forgive the hour.

What I can say that everyone already says: the Kökjal elders of the Toktogul basin hold the kamchy over the Naryn renewal. Their families were moved when the reservoir was filled. They will not consent to more drawdown without compensation for the pastures under the water.

In the city you will think this is about money. It is about the graves under the water, and fathers who were told in the 1970s that the water was progress. Money is only the language we have now for that.

The inner assembly sits by sanjyra, Karakoyun at the tör, as always. Talks all day. At night the young men play ulak and the old men pretend not to watch.
Day eleven. The horses are bored. The elders are not.

In Bishkek the papers say the observers are waiting in Tash-Kömür. Polite question only: does the Kurultai know the observers are waiting?
(I only ask. Please, I do not want the partition argument again.)
They know. The observers wait. The elders did not hurry for the Kokand khan either.

It is done. Nineteen days, the longest anyone here remembers.

Three elders from outside the reservoir lands, Biybolot Moldosh uulu leading, proposed that a fixed share of our side's Toktogul money go every year to a fund for the basin families, run by the Kökjal elders themselves. The Kökjal lifted the whip and stood aside. Nobody shouted. At the end an old woman sang a koshok for the drowned villages and the whole ring was quiet. I am not ashamed to say I wept.

Now it goes down to Tash-Kömür, to the commission and the observers, where people in shoes will take credit for it.
Thank you. In Nurzhan we will be warm this winter because of graves most of us never heard of. I will remember that every time the heating comes on.
Herald: Naryn schedule formally renewed to 2027 at Tash-Kömür. "The Kyrgyz delegation filed its customary written reservation."
Customary. Like the Kurultai. Everybody has their customs.
Diesel in the Chatkal villages: half again the Talas price. Same diesel. It just walked further.

To explain to the city people why this matters. Up here diesel is not for cars. It is the generator for the vaccine fridge, the pump, the one truck that brings flour before the snow. When the price goes up we do not drive less. We sell another sheep.

Soodagers bring it over the trails. They pay the clan levy, which is customary and written, and the elders read it out at the Kurultai. They also pay another levy at the line. Nobody reads that one out. The UNMI people say one fat-tailed sheep buys about 150 litres. That is the real exchange rate of Irad. Not five to the dollar.
Kenkol is closed again. Snow. Diesel up again. These two are married.
Kenkol open. Price not down. Divorce.

UNMI SAYS DIESEL IN CHATKAL VALLEY VILLAGES COSTS 40 TO 60 PERCENT MORE THAN IN TALAS. WE HAVE OUR OWN QUESTIONS ABOUT WHO PROFITS: [url=https://freeirad.org/diesel.html]The Gendarmerie's Diesel Empire[/url]. UNVERIFIED, AS ALWAYS. LABEL YOUR RUMOURS.

[quote=NotADPIagent]The ISEZ cannot be blamed for clan levies.[/quote]

threads.title: 2017 Abduction for Marriage Act: what changes in the villages

posts.body:
The legislature passed the Abduction for Marriage Act yesterday: 5 to 10 years in prison, up to 12 if she is under 18, and registry offices may not register a marriage that began with an abduction. The Ak Jooluk women watched the vote from the gallery.

My family is from Kara-Buura, where the case that started all this happened. I would like to hear from people in the villages and the valleys, not only from us in Toronto and Talas. What actually changes? Please keep it respectful.
An important thread. Note in advance: no names of anyone involved in any case, including the famous one. Speak about your villages, not your neighbours. Read the rules.

I have volunteered with Ak Jooluk since the Kyzyl-Adyr verdict. A fine. For taking a girl. A fine. That is what we were fighting.

The lawyer said it yesterday: a law is a beginning. A law is not a prosecutor. Now we watch the prosecutors.

For those who say this is "tradition": the Synod's 2014 pastoral letter On the Free Consent of Spouses calls bride kidnapping "a sin against the sacrament and against the dignity of women". Consent is what makes the marriage. Without it the crowning is a costume. A few village priests crowned such couples anyway, to keep the peace. That has to end too.

I am new and I post from the pasture, so slowly.

The act does not apply on our side of the line. The clan councils differ on whether a woman who was taken and stays is married. In my uruk the elders say a girl who says no goes home and kun is paid to her family. Some old men say ala kachuu was mostly staged elopement anyway. For some couples that is true. But I have sisters, and I know that "mostly" is a word men use.

Talas made a law and wants applause. Up here, what changes is when the grandmothers stop saying "she will get used to it". That is changing. Slowly. Not because of Talas.
A horse caught by force throws its rider for years. People are not less than horses.

Five years on. The TSU / St. Luka survey report is out: in the surveyed Talas Alatau and Karatau areas, 13% of married women under 50 began their marriage by abduction, about half of them unwillingly. Under 2% in the cities. Small sample, refused access, under-reporting, they say so themselves.
Prosecutions under the act: rare. We keep watching.
The Act is a great achievement of the DPI legislature. Have a nice day.
It is an achievement of the women who sat in the gallery. Have a nice day.

The IAC called the survey biased. Maybe it is. This spring a girl in our valley refused, and the elders sent her home with the kun paid. Five years ago that would have been a scandal. This year it was a conversation. I do not need a survey to see that.
half my dorm is from karatau. we talk about this at night sometimes. nobody i know would "get used to it". that's what changed

I am a herder in the Chatkal Highlands. In summer we are on the zhayloo, high up. The generator runs two hours in the evening: one hour for the vaccine fridge, one hour for this. My nephew tied a phone to a pole on the ridge.

I read you all winter at the kyshtoo. Now I will write sometimes. I will not tell you my clan. I will tell you that I have not trusted a Talas politician since 2007, when we rode into Talas with the Front, and that same summer the city was taken from under us by men in suits. I will not start trusting them because of a forum.

But I trust the people in this forum a little. You argue like a Kurultai.
Welcome. Save fuel. Write long.

From the winter house this time. Stone walls, felt on the walls, snow to the window. The road is closed until spring and the diesel is rationed, so the generator runs one hour now, for the radio and for this.

The young ones want to know what is happening in Talas. The old ones want to know what is happening with the sheep in the next valley. Both are right. Only one of them is on IradOne.

The book library came up to our camp last week, on two pack horses with wooden boxes. My daughter borrowed Akyrky Ashuu and read it to her grandmother by the lamp. Her grandmother knew the 1916 parts already, from her own grandmother. She corrected the novel twice.

Bektur says the IAC will not "negotiate with a recording". Up here the old men said the same thing in the summer. They judge a man by how he sits, and they say the man on IradOne sits like a picture.
RUMOUR, I know. We are not tech monitors. We are horse monitors.
Horses do not lie. Television is another animal.

Last post from the zhayloo this year, the herds go down next week.
My nephew asked if we should register for the free coins. His grandmother asked what you can buy with them. He said: nothing yet. She said: then it is a promise, and we already have a drawer full of those.

threads.title: Russian mobilization: our people in Moscow

posts.body:
Russia announced partial mobilization this morning. On our building site everybody is talking about nothing else.
I am on a Kyrgyz passport, they say that means I am not liable. My brother-in-law has a Russian passport since university. What do people know? Anyone with a lawyer?
My cousin in Yekaterinburg, Russian citizen since he studied there. This morning he put his wife and daughter on a bus to Nurzhan. He stays for the job. My aunt is not sleeping.
Nurzhan bus station is full every evening. Women with children and big checked bags. Some men come, some only say goodbye and go back.

Now recruiters come to the hostels. Contract service, big money, "citizenship fast". They come to guys with Kyrgyz passports, exactly the ones who are not liable. Some of the young ones are thinking about it.
The Department of Public Information advises ISEZ residents working in Russia not to sign any military contract.
First time I agree with him.

I know some people here think the diaspora should stay quiet about home. But this is about the boys, so I will say it. The fellow-countrymen's association in Moscow gives legal advice to migrants. Please, boys, call them before you sign anything at all. A contract is not a work permit. Your mothers want you home with ten fingers, not with a passport.
Update: brother-in-law got out through Kazakhstan, he is in Nurzhan now. Nobody on our site signed. I stay until December, then home. Thank you all.
Two years later. The rules for migrants in Russia are much tighter now, half our old brigade went to Almaty instead. I am in Nurzhan for good. Kobozev_Kid, is the refinery hiring?
Shift B is always hiring. Bring your own earplugs.

[quote=Ak_Shumkar]COME HOME.[/quote]
Their home is here, Ak. Their grandmother's home is Kara-Buura. The language is the bridge between. You can stand at one end and shout, or you can help build it.

My grandmother spoke Koryo-mar at home, Russian at work and Iradi at the bazaar. I speak Iradi, Russian and about four words of Korean. Language lives in the kitchen. Teach them to cook and to complain in Iradi. Grammar comes later.

Update after seven years: the class is 23 kids. Biggest recruiter: Karakush. Half of them came because of the "Ak Börü" dance and wanted to understand the words. I will take it. Tilge kaytuu, Toronto edition.
Last week a nine-year-old asked me why the American president wants to sell us. I did not have the words, in any language. Another girl, eight, said "Irad satylbayt". So the class is working.
